title: Reverse LL in group of given size K
stepTitle: Learn LinkedList [Single LL, Double LL, Medium, Hard Problems]
category: Learn LinkedList [Single LL, Double LL, Medium, Hard Problems]
problemStatement: Reverse the nodes of a linked list k at a time; leave a trailing group shorter than k untouched.
intuition: Reverse each full block with the standard three-pointer loop, then stitch the blocks back together. The bookkeeping — not the reversal — is the hard part, so use a dummy head and track the node before each group.

approaches.title: Optimal: check length, reverse block, reconnect
approaches.idea: group_prev holds the node before the current block.
approaches.dryRun:
1->2->3->4->5 k=2
block [1,2] reversed -> 2->1, connected to 3
block [3,4] reversed -> 4->3, connected to 5
[5] is short -> untouched
approaches.whyWorks: Reversing into group_next automatically links the block tail to the remaining list.

commonMistakes: Losing the connection between consecutive blocks
Not verifying that k nodes remain before reversing
patternRecognition: Block-wise pointer surgery — always verify the block exists before mutating
followUps: Reverse the trailing partial group too
interviewInsight: Reversing into group_next instead of None is the trick that removes most of the reconnection code.
